clue.text: Half a day with university intellectual is of great importance

indicators.note: only the first half of the weekday's name is kept, its second three letters dropped

parts.note: Monday is a day of the week
intellectual means mental, to do with the mind

explanation.surface: A scholar spending half a day at college is somehow treated as hugely significant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' cuts MONDAY to MON; this is a trimmed synonym, not letters printed in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something monumental is enormous in scale or significance, momentous.

clue.text: Handle roughly 1000 gold lines initially

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of the word lines

explanation.surface: Instructions for grabbing a thousand gold bars and the opening lines, perhaps of a heist.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to maul is to treat someone or something savagely, with rough hands.

clue.text: A trial, oddly, after profit rises and falls

indicators.note: after places the odd letters of 'A trial' behind the reversed profit word
in a down clue rising means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: profit means gain

indicators.note: oddly asks for the first, third and fifth letters of the words A and trial

explanation.surface: A court case goes strangely after someone's profits rise and fall, like a business story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falls' reads as a verb ending the surface but is the definition. In a down entry 'rises' means reading upward, and 'after' puts the 'oddly' picks behind the turned word.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Niagara Falls on the US-Canada border, so the proper name alone stands for the falls.

clue.text: Give a false account of various enterprises supporting millions

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means lying underneath, so the anagram goes below the M

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million(s)

indicators.note: various suggests the letters of enterprises are mixed into a different order

explanation.surface: A company report that inflates a range of businesses backed by millions in funding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' rearranges ENTERPRISES into ISREPRESENT; 'supporting' places that under M.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to misrepresent is to describe something falsely or misleadingly.

clue.text: Potential flier is irritating, taking son for first of trips

indicators.note: taking says one letter is brought in to stand where another was
for marks the swap: the son letter goes in place of the start of trips

parts.note: irritating means nettling, annoying

indicators.note: first of asks for the opening letter of the word trips

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A would-be pilot is annoying, bringing a son along instead of going on trips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking son for first of trips' swaps the first T of NETTLING for S.
explanation.definitionFit: A young bird not yet able to leave the nest will fly in time, so it is a flier in waiting.

clue.text: Grow old and cold in New York office

parts.note: to grow old is to age

indicators.note: in places the cold letter within the New York abbreviation

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone ageing and catching a chill while working in a Manhattan office.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an agency is a business or bureau, such as a government office or travel firm.

clue.text: Dog in film that is missing girl

indicators.note: missing says the abbreviation for that is is dropped from the dog's name

parts.note: Lassie is the collie of the famous films
IE (id est) is the abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: A film dog has gone missing, and so has a girl, like a news story.
explanation.walkthrough: Lassie is the rough collie of the 1943 film and its sequels.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lass is a Scottish and northern word for a young woman.

clue.text: Loving a party, make a call

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
to ring is to telephone

explanation.surface: Someone fond of a party picks up the phone to invite people.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: adoring means full of deep affection or worship.

clue.text: Replacements for spring on belt sent up

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring
re means on or concerning

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a strap is a belt

explanation.surface: Mechanic's notes: new springs on a drive belt, mounted upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: spare parts are components held in reserve to replace broken ones.

clue.text: It sends us off to protect area with no help

indicators.note: to protect means to wrap around, so the scrambled letters enclose the area letter
off suggests the letters are knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: A device that dispatches us to guard a zone with no backup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' rearranges ITSENDSUS into UNSSISTED; 'to protect' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: done unassisted means done alone, without any aid.

clue.text: Way of paying a final passage

parts.note: COD, cash on delivery, is a method of payment

explanation.surface: A payment method described as the last stage of a transaction.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical term: a coda is the closing section of a piece of music.

clue.text: Boastful Avon girl is worried, with proof of debts

indicators.note: worried suggests the letters of Avon girl are shaken into a new order

parts.note: IOUs, notes saying I owe you, are written evidence of debts

explanation.surface: An Avon saleswoman frets over her pile of debt notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' rearranges AVONGIRL into VAINGLOR; Avon is a cosmetics firm known for door-to-door saleswomen.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: vainglorious means excessively proud and given to bragging.

clue.text: Place of safety, mainly for a person of means

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a haven is a place of safety

explanation.surface: A refuge mostly reserved for the wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' drops the last letter of HAVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: in the phrase about rich and poor, a have is someone wealthy, one of the well-off.

clue.text: Profit-producing cure vital for redevelopment

indicators.note: redevelopment suggests the letters of cure vital are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A wonder remedy promises big returns once the scheme is redeveloped.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a lucrative venture makes plenty of money.

clue.text: Face alcohol before breakfast?

parts.note: suggests a morning drink, but means the scented lotion splashed on the face once the morning stubble is gone

explanation.surface: Someone reaching for a drink first thing in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Scented lotion applied to the face following a morning razor routine, typically spirit-based.

clue.text: Outrageous relative accommodated in apartment

indicators.note: accommodated in means housed inside, so the relative goes within the apartment word

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
gran, a grandmother, is a relative

explanation.surface: A scandalous situation: a relative moves into someone's flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: flagrant means glaring and shocking, as in a flagrant breach.

clue.text: Puzzle's new meaning missing at core

indicators.note: new suggests the remaining letters are made into a fresh arrangement
missing at core says the central letter of meaning is lost

explanation.surface: A puzzle whose fresh meaning lacks a central point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing at core' drops the middle N of MEANING, leaving MEAING; 'new' rearranges it. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an enigma is a mystery or riddle.

clue.text: Do nothing, say, to protect a good name

indicators.note: to protect means to surround, so the word for say wraps the other letters

parts.note: to say is to state

explanation.surface: Someone told to sit tight and speak up to shield their reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to stagnate is to stay idle and make no progress.

clue.text: Electronic circuits needing energy to go by

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
laps are circuits of a track
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: An electronics note: circuits need power before time can pass.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: time elapses when it passes.

clue.text: Gold relic designed for chamber

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: designed suggests the letters of relic are reshaped into a new form

explanation.surface: A golden relic made to sit in a chamber, perhaps a tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomy: an auricle is an atrium, an upper chamber of the heart.

clue.text: Surprise surrounding law-breaking champion

indicators.note: surrounding says the surprise word goes around the other letters

parts.note: a start is a sudden shock or surprise

indicators.note: breaking suggests the letters of law are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: A shocking twist: a champion caught breaking the law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Law-breaking' looks like one adjective but splits into fodder and signal: 'breaking' scrambles it to LWA, which 'surrounding' tells the surprise word to enclose.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a stalwart is a loyal supporter, someone who champions a cause.

clue.text: A row about the Spanish studio

indicators.note: about means going around, so the row word wraps the Spanish article

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A quarrel over the Spanish artist's workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an atelier is an artist's or designer's workshop.

clue.text: House accommodating a bad-tempered woman

indicators.note: accommodating means giving room to, so the house word holds the a

parts.note: Virgo is one of the twelve astrological houses, the signs of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A house taking in a grumpy female lodger.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a virago is a domineering, shrewish woman.

clue.text: Abandoning reputation to protect daughter at last

indicators.note: to protect means to surround, so the reputation word wraps the letter

parts.note: standing is reputation or status

indicators.note: at last asks for the final letter of the word daughter

explanation.surface: A parent giving up their good name to shield a daughter in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: stranding someone is leaving them stuck and deserted.

clue.text: Grass as part of fat-free diet

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Grass recommended as part of a low-fat diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: reeds are tall grasses growing in wetlands.

clue.text: Place causing a bit of travel sickness on the way back?

indicators.note: on the way back says the hidden letters are read backwards
a bit of says only some letters inside the following words are taken

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A spot that brings on mild nausea on the return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'Place causing a bit' swallowed the signal: 'a bit of' marks the letters taken from 'travel sickness', and 'causing' is a link, so the definition is 'Place'.
explanation.definitionFit: An island is a kind of place, a piece of land in the sea.

clue.text: Span of religion primarily found in a church

indicators.note: found in says the picked letter sits inside the other pieces
primarily asks for the opening letter of the word religion

explanation.surface: The span of a faith, chiefly seen within one church.
explanation.definitionFit: Architecture: an arch is a curved structure spanning an opening.

clue.text: Facilities offered by politicians after volcanic outpouring?

indicators.note: after puts the politicians behind the volcanic word

parts.note: lava is the molten rock a volcano pours out
Tories are members of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Amenities laid on by politicians once an eruption has subsided.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphemism: facilities is a polite word for toilets.

clue.text: Always strict, dismissing outsiders

indicators.note: dismissing outsiders says the first and last letters of the strict word are dropped

parts.note: severe means strict

explanation.surface: A permanently strict boss who sacks anyone from outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: ever means at all times, forever.

clue.text: Authorities encourage rapid increase in electricity used

parts.note: powers are authorities, as in the powers that be
to urge is to encourage

explanation.surface: The authorities push for a quick rise in electricity consumption.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden spike in mains current or voltage, often damaging to appliances.
